content.text:
# Recursion Explained for Beginners

Recursion is when a function calls itself to solve a problem by breaking it down into smaller, similar sub-problems. Each time the function calls itself, it works with a simpler version of the original problem, getting closer to a basic case that it can solve directly. The function must have a "base case"—a simple condition where it stops calling itself and returns a direct answer—otherwise it would call itself forever. Once the base case is reached, the function returns its answer back up through all the previous function calls, building up the final result.
